primitives.name: Vercel Project Linkage Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: The ".vercel" folder is created when you link a directory to a Vercel project.
primitives.assumptions: Directory linking is deterministic and idempotent; .vercel folder is ephemeral to project state.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When project unlinking occurs, folder deletion triggers state collapse.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's authorization state space where P(orgId|projectId) defines access kernel; to GSE's state transition graph where folder persistence implies committed state.

primitives.name: Project Metadata Storage Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: The "project.json" file contains: - The ID of the Vercel project that you linked ("projectId") - The ID of the user or team your Vercel project is owned by ("orgId") > Should I commit the ".vercel" folder?
primitives.assumptions: Metadata integrity is preserved under atomic write operations; data is immutable post-write.
primitives.breakdown_regime: On unauthorized access, metadata becomes invalid due to mismatched orgId.

layer2.mapping: Derives into GSI's credential validation logic; informs GSE's state consistency checks.

primitives.name: Folder Compliance Policy
primitives.verbatim_quote: No, you should not share the ".vercel" folder with anyone.
primitives.assumptions: Sharing is a violation of access control policy; folder is private to owner.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If shared, compliance fails and triggers audit alert.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's access control model; to GSE's policy enforcement engine.
